title: Katun Smoke and Lynx Country: A Šar-Mavrovo-Galičica Cabin Week

bestPeriod.avoid: November-April, the Bistra and Šar tracks are snow-blocked, Galičnik empties to two residents, and the Korab border zone is effectively shut

accommodation.note: Village guesthouses 1,800-3,000 MKD (€29, €49) a double; mountain lodges and katun nights cheaper

food.note: Mehana mains 350-600 MKD (€6, €10); two self-catered nights on the plateau

transport.note: High-clearance rental €45, €65/day, fuel around 80 MKD/litre (€1.30), no motorway vignette

activities.note: Park tickets, Bigorski donation, a guided Korab day or lynx-corridor morning, Sveti Naum spring boat

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5, one 1,300 m ascent day on Korab; the rest is 8-14 km at moderate gradient, but shepherd tracks and karst make the going slower than the map suggests

gatewayAirport: SKP Skopje, 1 h 50 to Mavrovi Anovi and 1 h 10 to Popova Šapka; OHD Ohrid, 25 min to the Galičica gate and 2 h 15 to Mavrovo
summary: North Macedonia keeps its wildest ground in a north-south chain of limestone and old forest that almost nobody outside the Balkans walks: Šar Planina, made a national park only in 2021, then Mavrovo's 73,000 hectares of beech and spruce around an artificial lake with a drowned church in it, then Galičica riding the ridge between Ohrid and Prespa. This week moves down that chain slowly. You sleep in a shepherd's katun on the Bistra plateau, in a stone house in Galičnik where two people live year-round, and finally on the Ohrid shore. The centrepiece is Korab at 2,764 m, the country's high point, sitting exactly on the Albanian border, reached through a military-controlled zone. Around it are deliberately empty days: the Radika river, a monastery with the most extravagant carved iconostasis in the Balkans, and an afternoon spent watching a plateau do nothing. It suits people who like wood smoke, cash economies and the knowledge that the last confirmed stronghold of the Balkan lynx is in the forest below them.

itinerary.title: Šar Planina from Popova Šapka
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Skopje and drive west on the A2 to Tetovo, then up the switchback road to Popova Šapka at about 1,750 m, the old ski village that is the only vehicle access into Šar Planina National Park, designated in 2021 and still the least-developed park in the country. Buy bread, cheese and ajvar in Tetovo's bazaar before you climb.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk out along the grassy ridge towards Ceripašina and the Titov Vrv approach (2,748 m, the park's high point and a full day in itself). Two to three hours out and back gives you the whole Polog plain on one side and a sea of empty 2,500 m humps on the other, plus working sheepfolds and their dogs.
itinerary.evening: Eat in one of the Popova Šapka lodges, grilled lamb, šopska salad, and the local rakija poured without being asked. Cash.
itinerary.dayStats: 65 km drive / 1 h 10 / Popova Šapka 1,750 m / 8-10 km ridge walk, 350 m ascent / Šar Planina NP 62,705 ha, declared 2021
itinerary.sleep: Lodge or apartment at Popova Šapka

itinerary.title: Down to Mavrovo and the drowned church
itinerary.morning: Descend to Gostivar and continue to Mavrovi Anovi. Mavrovo Lake is an artificial reservoir filled in the early 1950s, and when the level drops, usually late summer and autumn, the church of Sveti Nikola, built in 1850 and flooded when the valley was dammed, stands clear of the water with its walls stained to the high-water line. In a wet year you see only the bell tower.
itinerary.afternoon: Slow the pace. Walk the lake shore path, call in at the Mavrovo NP office in Mavrovi Anovi to ask about track conditions on Bistra and whether any fire ban is in force, and fill the car and every water container at the Makpetrol station, the last fuel before the plateau.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at the hotel restaurant on the lake; trout, tavče gravče, and the flat local flija if anyone is making it.
itinerary.dayStats: 78 km drive / 1 h 30 / Mavrovo NP 73,088 ha, founded 1949 / lake surface roughly 13 km² / last fuel and full shop for 3 days
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Bistra or Hotel Tutto, Mavrovo

itinerary.title: Bistra plateau and a night at the katuns
itinerary.morning: Drive to Nikiforovo and take the shepherd track up onto Bistra, a broad limestone plateau of sinkholes and grass at 1,600-2,100 m. Go slowly; this is the surface that turns to grease after rain. Park at the last turning circle and walk in to the katun cluster.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk up to Medenica (2,163 m), the plateau's high point, for the whole Korab wall to the west. The katuns, seasonal stone-and-timber shepherd huts occupied roughly June to September, are working buildings, not attractions: ask before entering, buy cheese, and expect to be fed whether you asked or not.
itinerary.evening: Wood stove, candlelight, and the plateau going completely silent after the flocks are penned. Cook what you carried. The Milky Way here is startling; the nearest street light is 20 km away.
itinerary.dayStats: 20 km, last 11 km unsealed / 40 min drive at walking pace / katuns 1,750-1,900 m / Medenica 2,163 m / no signal, no shop, no power
itinerary.sleep: Katun or restored plateau hut, Bistra (arranged through the park office or a Nikiforovo driver)

itinerary.title: Galičnik, and a genuinely slow day
itinerary.morning: Come off the plateau to Galičnik, a stone village at 1,400 m built by Mijak shepherds who wintered their flocks as far away as Thessaly. Two people live here year-round. Walk the empty lanes, the slate roofs, the church of Sveti Petar and Pavle, and the cemetery terraces above.
itinerary.afternoon: Do nothing on purpose. Read on a terrace. If you are here on 12 July, Petrovden, the Galičnik Wedding festival brings a real couple, zurla and tapan players and about 5,000 visitors to a village that has two residents, book a bed months out or come as a day trip from Mavrovo. One or two days before it, the shepherds' gathering at Smrdliva Voda holds shearing and milking contests and a Šarplaninec dog parade.
itinerary.evening: Dinner is whatever the guesthouse cooks, usually pastrmajlija or slow lamb, eaten at one table with everyone else staying.
itinerary.dayStats: 22 km drive / Galičnik 1,400 m / 2 permanent residents / wedding festival held around 12 July, roughly 5,000 attendees / August art colony, founded 1990
itinerary.sleep: Neda Guest House or a village konak, Galičnik

itinerary.title: Korab, the country's roof
itinerary.morning: A pre-dawn start. The classic Macedonian ascent leaves from Strezimir/Džepište above Debar, on a 4x4 track, then climbs past the Korab waterfall, a 130 m-plus seasonal fall, among the highest in the Balkans, thin by late summer, to the ridge and the summit cairn at 2,764 m, the high point of both North Macedonia and Albania. The whole line lies inside a border zone: you need permission from the interior ministry arranged in advance, and going with a guide or with the organised mass ascent is the only frictionless way to do it.
itinerary.afternoon: The annual mass ascent falls in the first days of September, tied to the 8 September independence holiday, when the border zone is opened collectively and several thousand people walk up together. Outside that weekend, the Albanian side from Radomirë above Peshkopi is administratively simpler but requires a legal border crossing and a rental car cleared for Albania.
itinerary.evening: Off the hill by late afternoon, down to Debar or the Radika for grilled meat and a beer you have genuinely earned.
itinerary.dayStats: 16-18 km round trip / 1,250-1,400 m ascent / 8-10 h / summit 2,764 m / border-zone permit required; mass ascent in early September / no water above the last spring, carry 3 L
itinerary.sleep: Guesthouse at Janče or Rostuše, Radika valley

itinerary.title: Radika, Bigorski, and the drive south
itinerary.morning: A deliberately light day. Sveti Jovan Bigorski monastery, founded in the 11th century and rebuilt many times, holds a walnut iconostasis carved between 1829 and 1835 by Petre Filipovski Garkata and Makarij Frčkovski, the most ambitious woodcarving in the region, with hundreds of figures. Dress modestly; photography rules vary and are enforced.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive south past Debar and along the Crn Drim to Struga and around to the Galičica gate. Stop for the Duf waterfall above Rostuše if the legs allow, 20 minutes up a gorge path from the village.
itinerary.evening: Arrive at Sveti Naum in the last of the light, when the coaches have gone. Dinner of Ohrid trout or plaška, and note that the endemic Ohrid trout is subject to catch restrictions, so ask what you are actually being served.
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km drive / 2 h 45 / Bigorski iconostasis carved 1829-1835 / Galičica NP founded 1958, day ticket 100 MKD (about €1.60) / vehicle and camping tickets extra: tent up to 4 people 300 MKD, camper 400 MKD, ATV 500 MKD
itinerary.sleep: Monastery guest rooms at Sveti Naum, or a Ljubaništa guesthouse

itinerary.title: Galičica saddle, Prespa, and out
itinerary.morning: Walk the Sveti Naum springs first thing, dozens of karst vents feeding the Crn Drim, cold and blue, best seen from a rowing boat before 09:00. Then take the saddle road that crosses Galičica between the two lakes, climbing from the Ohrid shore to about 1,600 m at the pass.
itinerary.afternoon: From the saddle, walk part of the ridge towards Magaro (2,254 m) for the view that defines the park: Ohrid on one side, Prespa 155 m lower on the other, and the water moving underground between them through the limestone. Drop to the Prespa shore at Otešovo or Konjsko for a last swim.
itinerary.evening: Back to Ohrid for dinner in the old town, then OHD, 15 minutes away, or the 2 h 45 run to Skopje.
itinerary.dayStats: Galičica saddle road tops out near 1,600 m / Magaro 2,254 m / Ohrid 695 m, Prespa 850 m, a 155 m difference drained through karst / OHD 15 min from Ohrid, SKP 2 h 45
itinerary.sleep: Ohrid, or an airport hotel at Skopje

accommodationStrategy.name: A Bistra katun or restored plateau hut
accommodationStrategy.description: The defining night of the week: stone walls, a wood stove, spring water in a hosepipe, and a plateau that goes absolutely quiet at dusk. These are arranged informally through the Mavrovo NP office or a Nikiforovo driver rather than booked online, they are seasonal (roughly late June to mid-September), and payment is cash. Bring a sleeping bag, a head torch and all your food.

accommodationStrategy.name: Neda Guest House / a village konak
accommodationStrategy.description: Galičnik's guesthouse tradition is the reason the village is not a ruin. Expect a room in a restored Mijak house, breakfast of homemade cheese and pastry, and a host who will explain the wedding customs whether or not it is July. Roughly 1,800-3,000 MKD (€29, €49) a double. Book months ahead for the 12 July festival; the rest of the summer is walk-in.

accommodationStrategy.name: Sveti Naum monastery guest rooms
accommodationStrategy.description: The monastery complex, founded around 905, rents simple rooms inside the walls. The point is the two hours after the last day-trip coach leaves and the two before the first arrives, when the springs and the lakeshore are yours. Around €50, €80 a double in season, and the only quiet accommodation at the southern end of the lake.

logistics.connectivity: North Macedonia is not in the EU, so EU roam-like-home does not apply. Western Balkans operators run a regional roam-like-at-home scheme among themselves, and EU-Western Balkans rates were cut in late 2023, but you can still be charged. A local prepaid SIM from A1 or Telekom costs a few hundred denars with several gigabytes and is the cheap answer. Coverage fails entirely in the Radika gorge, on Bistra, and on the Korab approach.
logistics.emergency: 112 for everything; it dispatches the Mountain Rescue Service (Gorska Služba za Spasuvanje), whose teams are volunteer and concentrated around Skopje, Tetovo and Ohrid. Response into Bistra or the Korab border zone is measured in hours, not minutes. Insurance must name mountaineering above 2,500 m and helicopter evacuation, and North Macedonia is outside the EHIC/GHIC system, you are paying up front and claiming back.
logistics.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms build over the Šar and Korab ridges from roughly 14:00 in June-August and arrive fast; there is no shelter on either. The Bistra plateau fogs in with almost no warning, and it is featureless enough to get genuinely lost in, carry a compass as well as a phone. Snow patches survive in the Korab north-facing gullies into late June.
logistics.bookingWindows: Galičnik for the July wedding needs booking three to six months ahead; the mass Korab ascent in early September is organised through the mountaineering federation and registration closes weeks in advance. The interior-ministry border-zone permit for Korab outside that event should be started at least two to three weeks before travel and is easiest through a licensed guide. Katun nights are arranged days ahead, not months.
logistics.money: The denar (MKD) is pegged at roughly 61.5 to the euro; think of 100 MKD as €1.60. Cards work in Skopje, Ohrid and hotel restaurants, and nowhere else that matters on this trip. Draw cash in Gostivar or Debar and carry 8,000-12,000 MKD in small notes for guesthouses, katuns, fuel and park tickets. Tipping is rounding up, or 10% for a proper sit-down meal.
logistics.transportRules: There is no vignette; the A1 and A2 motorways are tolled at barriers, cash or card, in small amounts. Rental contracts frequently exclude unsealed roads, the Bistra and Strezimir tracks are exactly what that clause is written for, so declare your plans and pay for the right vehicle. Taking a Macedonian rental into Albania needs the agency's written permission plus a green card, and not every desk allows it; if you intend the Albanian side of Korab, arrange that at booking.
logistics.permits: Galičica NP charges 100 MKD (about €1.60) per person per day, with separate tickets for vehicles, tents and campers. Mavrovo and Šar Planina do not gate general access but charge for specific activities and camping. Wild camping outside designated areas is not permitted in the parks. Drone flight needs Civil Aviation Agency authorisation and is restricted over parks and anywhere near the border zone, do not fly on Korab under any circumstances. Foraging is banned in park core zones; commercial collection needs a Makedonski Šumi permit.
logistics.health: Town tap water is generally potable; spring and hosepipe water on the plateau should be filtered or boiled, particularly below grazing. Ticks are abundant April-October in the beech belt, check nightly. Nose-horned viper lives on sunny scree throughout the region; antivenom is in the hospitals, not the mountains. Livestock guard dogs are the most likely injury on this trip: stop, do not run, keep the vehicle or a stick between you, and let the shepherd call them off.

proTips: Call the Mavrovo NP office before committing to the Bistra night and ask two questions: whether the Nikiforovo track has dried out, and whether an open-fire ban is currently in force. Both change weekly in summer.

If you want Korab without the paperwork, aim for the mass ascent in the first days of September, the border zone is opened collectively, the atmosphere is a national holiday on a mountain, and you will still be alone for most of the descent.
Buy cheese directly at a Bistra katun. It is the cheapest and best thing you will eat all week, and paying cash for it is the whole basis on which visitors are welcome up there.
Visit Sveti Naum's springs before 09:00 or after 18:00. Between those hours it is the single busiest coach stop in the country.
Galičnik on 12 July is spectacular and impossible; Galičnik on 12 August is the same village with nobody in it and every guesthouse free. Choose deliberately.
Draw all your cash in Gostivar or Debar. There is no ATM in Galičnik, none on Bistra, and the machine at Mavrovi Anovi is unreliable in season.
Take the Galičica saddle road east to west in the late afternoon: the light comes off Prespa onto the limestone, and the Ohrid descent puts the lake in front of you the whole way down.
Early September is the best single week here, beech mast pulls bears low, porcini are up in the Mavrovo forests, the katuns are still occupied, and the mass Korab ascent falls in the same window.

raw.Remote access, the tracks that matter: The Bistra plateau is reached from Mavrovi Anovi by 9 km of asphalt to Nikiforovo, then roughly 11 km of unsealed shepherd track towards the Sultanica and Trnica summer pastures. Dry, a high-clearance estate manages it at 15 km/h; after a summer storm the clay ruts and only a genuine 4x4 gets out again, the plateau drains badly and stays greasy for a day or two. The Galičnik approach is asphalt for all 17 km from Mavrovi Anovi but single-lane, blind-cornered and unlit. The Korab approach on the Macedonian side runs from Debar up the Dolna Reka to Strezimir and Džepište, the last 12 km on a broken forest track that is 4x4-only and impassable with snow patches into June. The Albanian alternative, Radomirë-Cereni above Peshkopi, is 8 km of rocky 4x4 track from the village to the meadows below the ridge.
raw.Last-mile walk-ins and transfers: The katun cluster below Medenica (2,163 m) is a 25-40 minute walk from the last turning circle, carry a rucksack, not a case. Galičnik's upper lanes are cobbled and steep; park at the village entrance and walk 200-400 m. The Mavrovo park office in Mavrovi Anovi (npmavrovo.org.mk) will put you in touch with local drivers who run Land Cruisers to the pastures and to the Korab trailhead; in Debar and Rostuše, arrangements are informal, cash, and settled the night before.
raw.Wilderness isolation, Level 4 of 5 on Bi: From the Bistra katuns it is roughly 35-40 minutes of track to paved road at Nikiforovo, no permanent neighbours within 5 km outside the June-September grazing season, nearest shop and fuel at the Makpetrol station in Mavrovi Anovi (about 20 km, closes early), nearest pharmacy in Gostivar (55 km), nearest hospital the general hospital in Gostivar, about 1 h 10 from the plateau. Galičnik sits at Level 3: paved road all the way, but two permanent residents in winter, no shop, and 40 minutes to Mavrovi Anovi. Galičica drops to Level 2, Ohrid and its hospital are within 40 minutes of the whole park.
raw.Off-grid reality: The katuns and the restored huts are solar-lit at best, most often candle and head torch; the working sheepfolds run small generators for the milking machines only. Water comes from spring boxes and hosepipes fed by karst sources, locals drink it untreated, and you should still filter or boil, especially downstream of grazing. Heat and cooking are wood-stove; firewood is stacked and you replace what you burn. Toilets are long-drop; grey water goes on the ground away from the spring. Bring everything: there is no shop between Mavrovi Anovi and Galičnik, none at all on Bistra, and Debar's supermarkets close by 20:00.
raw.Phone signal: Patchy A1 and Telekom coverage on the Bistra ridgelines, nothing in the Radika gorge or the katun hollows, none at all on the Korab approach until you are on the summit ridge where Albanian networks bleed across. Galičica's saddle road has good coverage. Download offline maps for the whole chain before leaving Skopje, the shepherd tracks are not on standard car navigation.
raw.Foraging rules: North Macedonia is a serious wild-mushroom exporter, and the working distinction is personal versus commercial. Commercial collection needs a permit or contract through Makedonski Šumi, the state forest enterprise, and protected wild species need authorisation from the environment ministry; casual picking for the pot in ordinary state forest is tolerated. Collection is prohibited outright in national park core-protection zones, that means the Mavrovo, Galičica and Šar Planina strict zones, which are signposted only intermittently, so ask a ranger before you fill a basket. Peak season is September-November for porcini (*varganj*) and chanterelles (*lisičarka*), with morels in spring. There is no public mycological inspection service for tourists; the practical equivalent is the *otkupen punkt*, the village buying station, where the buyer sorts commercial hauls and will look at yours. Never pick, cut or dig protected endemics, the Šar and Galičica ridges hold a long list of them.
raw.Named places to sleep and their characte: Galičnik is a stone amphitheatre of slate roofs with one guesthouse tradition (Neda's house is the long-standing one), loud for the July wedding, silent otherwise. Hotel Bistra and Hotel Tutto at Mavrovo lake are ski hotels that stay open in summer at half price. Hotel Radika at Nikiforovo sits closest to the Bistra tracks; the restored han at Janče is the Radika's atmospheric choice; and the guest wing inside the Sveti Naum monastery complex puts you above the springs after the buses leave.
raw.Wildlife: Mavrovo is the core range of the Balkan lynx (*Lynx lynx balcanicus*), estimated at fewer than 40 mature individuals subspecies-wide and monitored for over a decade by camera trap under the Balkan Lynx Recovery Programme (Macedonian Ecological Society, with PPNEA in Albania). Your chance of seeing one is close to zero; treat prints in the Radika mud as the sighting. Brown bear and grey wolf use the Bistra-Korab corridor at dawn and dusk, feeding on beech mast in September-October; chamois hold the Korab and Šar cliffs. Ethical rules: no baiting, no call playback, no drones over ridges, dogs on leads near sheepfolds. Organise anything guided through the park offices or a licensed mountain guide, not an ad-hoc driver.
raw.Fire and open flame: Summer fire risk in western Macedonia is high and the government routinely declares 30-day nationwide bans on open fires in and near forest during June-August, with real fines and, in bad years, an emergency crisis state. Assume cooking on stoves and existing fireplaces only, never on the plateau grass, and note that the Bistra pastures are burned deliberately by shepherds in places, do not add to it.

sources.confidenceNotes: The Korab border-zone permit procedure, its lead time, and the 2026 date and registration route for the mass ascent are the most volatile facts in the file, re-verify with the Ministry of the Interior and the mountaineering federation. The Strezimir/Džepište track condition changes every season. No statutory personal-use kilogram limit for mushrooms was confirmed for North Macedonia this run; the file describes the permit structure rather than quoting a number, and a checked figure should be inserted before publication. Bistra katun availability and price were not confirmed against a live source, treat as locally arranged and verify with the Mavrovo NP office. Guesthouse names in Galičnik and Popova Šapka and the Sveti Naum room rate need current confirmation. Korab waterfall height is reported variously between about 100 m and 138 m. Fuel price and the MKD peg should be refreshed at publication.
